Article.ArticleTitle: Surgical approaches and long-term outcomes in adults with complex re-operative hypospadias repair.

Abstract.AbstractText: Patients with failed hypospadias repair are a challenging population for both pediatric and reconstructive urologists. In this study, we describe our long-term outcomes and factors associated with complications in repeat hypospadias repairs.

A retrospective review of 32 adult patients with a history of hypospadias repair who required subsequent urethroplasty between 2002 and 2012 was performed. Presenting complaint, past medical and surgical history, demographic data, surgical approach, intraoperative findings, and complications were collected and analyzed.

Median age at the time of urethroplasty was 32 years. Stricture of the penile urethra was the most common presentation. 30 patients underwent urethroplasty for stricture treatment, 1 patient had a perineal urethrostomy, and 1 had a diverticulectomy. Of those who underwent urethroplasty 90% had a two-staged repair. Initial success rate was 83% in patients who underwent one- or two-stage urethroplasty. After a median follow-up of 9.5 years, complications included 4 recurrent strictures and 1 fistula. Age of patient, previous interventions, length of stricture, hair present at the time of repair, the need to excise the urethral plate, and the number of stages were not associated with complications or recurrence. If a graft was required, the use of skin was significantly associated with recurrence compared to buccal mucosa.

Excellent outcomes can be achieved using a two-staged approach with replacement or augmentation of the urethral plate in adults with failed hypospadias repair. In our experience, buccal mucosa appears to be associated with fewer complications and stricture recurrence than skin grafts.
